questions.question: What does the subscript 2 in H₂O indicate?
What does the coefficient 3 in 3CO₂ indicate?
choices: Three carbon dioxide molecules or three moles, depending on scale
Three oxygen atoms in each molecule
Three carbon atoms in each molecule

questions.question: What is the formula for sodium chloride?
Which name corresponds to CO₂?

A bonded group of atoms with a net charge

questions.question: What does a Roman numeral in iron(III) chloride specify?
choices: The number of iron atoms in every molecule

questions.question: Which ion is represented by OH⁻?
Why must an ionic compound's formula balance ionic charges?

Only the negative ions contribute charge

questions.question: Why do molecular names use prefixes such as di- and tri-?
choices: They identify numbers of atoms of particular elements

questions.question: Why is MgCl₂ the simplest formula for magnesium chloride?
choices: One Mg²⁺ balances two Cl⁻ ions
The compound must contain equal atom counts

questions.question: How does FeCl₂ differ from FeCl₃ in the usual ionic model?

They must have identical iron oxidation states
They contain iron ions with different charges

questions.question: What does placing parentheses around a polyatomic ion mean when a subscript follows?
choices: The subscript applies to the entire enclosed group
The subscript applies only to the first symbol

questions.question: Why does changing H₂O to H₂O₂ change the substance?
choices: It merely changes how many water molecules are present
It changes only the sample size
It changes the ratio of hydrogen to oxygen atoms

questions.question: Why do ionic formulas commonly show simplest ratios rather than discrete molecules?
choices: Every ionic solid is a gas
Ionic formulas describe electron paths only
Ionic solids form extended lattices of ions

questions.question: Why is the symbol Co different from CO?
choices: Co names cobalt; CO represents carbon monoxide
Capitalization does not affect chemical symbols
